lines.text: On roofs, on roads, on parking lots.
And almost none of it soaks in.
On a forest floor, about one drop in ten runs off.
In a dense city, more than half does.
On the way, it picks up oil, tyre dust and fertiliser,
and storm drains carry it, often untreated, into the river.
But there is a gentle fix.
A rain garden: a shallow, planted dip, where runoff already flows.
After a storm, water pools on top.
A sandy soil mix filters the rest. Microbes break down oil, and roots take up nutrients.
Cleaner water seeps down, to recharge the groundwater.
In a day or two it's dry again, too soon for mosquitoes to breed.
One garden is small. Street by street, they make a city a sponge again.
It can start with the rain on your own roof.
